name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,551

clue.text: Head off in top health after training for sporting event

indicators.note: taking the head off a word means dropping its opening letter
training knocks raw material into a new shape, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the little word in with its first letter removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: An athlete trains hard to reach peak fitness ahead of a big competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' reads like an instruction to set out, but it beheads the word in.
explanation.definitionFit: The heptathlon is an athletics competition of seven disciplines, so it is one example of a sporting contest.

clue.text: Kairos is sadly upset with seasoned food

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting something turns it upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Kairos is the setter, so 'Kairos is' becomes 'I'm' from the setter's mouth
alas is an expression of sorrow

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to feeling down while eating some spicy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter naming themselves stands for I or ME; here 'Kairos is' gives I'M, and with ALAS the whole lot is turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured sausage flavoured heavily with garlic and spices, so it qualifies as highly flavoured fare.

clue.text: Benevolent group of creatures in Dr Who

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for group, as in G7 or G20
the Ood are a tentacle-faced alien race in the BBC science-fiction series Doctor Who

explanation.surface: A kindly band of aliens appears in the long-running science-fiction television show.
explanation.walkthrough: You need to know the Ood, a race of gentle servant aliens from Doctor Who, the long-running BBC series.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone benevolent is kind and well-meaning, and being kind is one plain meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Home counties in secret compact

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: closet as an adjective means kept private, as in a closet fan
the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A clandestine agreement is struck among the shires around London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compact' looks like the noun for a pact, which suits the surface, but it is the adjective: tightly packed.
explanation.definitionFit: Things set closely together with little space between them are densely packed, which is what compact describes.

clue.text: Handle head on the phone

indicators.note: on a telephone line you only hear a word, never see its spelling

blocks.note: nob is old slang for the head

explanation.surface: Someone in charge deals with a matter during a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' and 'head' both look like verbs about managing something; one is a noun for a door grip and the other is slang for the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded knob on a door or drawer is the part you grip to open it, so it is a type of grip.

clue.text: Look after worker with short fat animal

indicators.note: one piece coming after the others means it is placed at the end
cutting a word short means dropping its final letter

blocks.note: a worker bee is the stock crossword worker
the word fat with its last letter cut
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone is told to care for an overweight employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A beefalo is a cross between domestic cattle and the American bison, bred for meat, so it is a livestock creature.

clue.text: Parts of blackbird in stream

blocks.note: the first part, black, gives B, the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
the second part, bird, gives a rook, a black bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: Pieces of a dead blackbird are found floating in a creek.
explanation.walkthrough: The compound word blackbird is split into its two halves, black and bird, and each is clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook is a small natural watercourse, so it is a synonym for a little creek or rivulet.

clue.text: Boys touring navy docks

indicators.note: touring something means going all the way round it, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: lads are boys
N is the abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: Young sailors take a tour of the naval shipyards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docks' looks like the noun for harbours; it is the verb, as a ship docks.
explanation.definitionFit: When a ship docks it comes in to shore and lands, so both verbs mean arriving at port.

clue.text: Bust-up over extra underlying theme

indicators.note: a bust-up is a violent quarrel, and something broken up is scrambled into disorder
in a down clue, one piece over another is placed above it

blocks.note: the letters of bust rearranged
ext. is a dictionary abbreviation for extra

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over an additional charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtext is the implicit meaning lying beneath the words of a text, so it is the hidden theme beneath.

clue.text: Extremely tense noise

blocks.note: too means excessively
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like the outer-letters signal for tense; it is the word too.
explanation.definitionFit: A toot is a short blast from a horn or whistle, so it is a kind of sound.

clue.text: A theologian is with a couple of graduates in capital city

blocks.note: taken as written
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theology degree
taken as written
taken as written
two BAs, Bachelor of Arts being the stock graduate

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar joins two university alumni in some metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the seat of government of Ethiopia, making it that nation's capital.

clue.text: Nervous runner times his running

indicators.note: running here means in motion and out of place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a ski is a runner that slides over snow, as on a sledge
T is time, so times is two of them
the letters of his rearranged

explanation.surface: An anxious athlete checks his lap times while jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like an athlete, matching the surface, but it is a ski, which runs on snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A skittish horse or person is easily startled and jumpy, which is a close synonym of anxious.

clue.text: Add lines to plan

blocks.note: first meaning: to shade a drawing with fine parallel lines
second meaning: to devise a scheme or plot

explanation.surface: Someone extends a scheme by writing extra lines into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists shade drawings with close parallel strokes, and conspirators devise a plot; the one verb covers both activities.

clue.text: Second piece moving left to right

indicators.note: left stands for the letter L, and shifting it rightwards changes the letter order

blocks.note: a sliver is a thin piece

explanation.surface: A chess or board-game player shifts another piece across the board.
explanation.walkthrough: L is left; in SLIVER it moves one place right to give SILVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is the medal awarded for coming second, so the metal stands for runner-up place.

clue.text: Sell iodine prepared as a preservative

indicators.note: something prepared is made up from ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemist markets iodine solution as something that keeps things from decaying.
explanation.definitionFit: Linseed oil, pressed from flax seed, is rubbed into wood and cricket bats to protect them from rot and drying out.

clue.text: Relax after Charlie leaves English comedian?

indicators.note: Charlie is the radio code for C, and that letter leaving means it is taken out

blocks.note: to chill is to relax

explanation.surface: An English comic unwinds once his friend Charlie has gone home.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet. The question mark flags that the definition is by example: Benny Hill and Harry Hill are both English comedians.
explanation.definitionFit: Benny Hill and Harry Hill are well-known British comics, so the surname stands for one such funny man.

clue.text: Raids in Mediterranean island reported

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so what counts is how the words sound

blocks.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: News comes of attacks on a holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are hostile incursions into enemy territory, the older military sense, so they match attacks.

clue.text: Composition of note pig thief returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
in the nursery rhyme, Tom the piper's son stole a pig

explanation.surface: A piece of music is composed about a stolen pig being given back.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Tom, Tom, the piper's son, stole a pig and away he run' supplies the thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short choral piece, usually sacred, so it is a kind of musical work.

clue.text: Short run on TV omitting province's woes

indicators.note: omitting something means leaving it out of the word

blocks.note: a drama shown in a small number of episodes
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A brief television drama leaves out a region's troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK, Northern Ireland is commonly referred to simply as the Province.
explanation.definitionFit: Miseries are hardships and sorrows, and the plural noun is a direct synonym of troubles.

clue.text: Makes money from Cabernet Sauvignon

indicators.note: letters taken from a phrase are lifted out of it intact

blocks.note: found running across the two words of the wine name

explanation.surface: A vineyard turns a profit from selling a red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To net an amount is to earn it as clear profit after costs, so the verb means taking home income.

clue.text: Varieties of African bread found in Bahamas

indicators.note: something found in a place is sitting inside it

blocks.note: BS is the international vehicle code for the Bahamas
bread is slang for money, and the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: Kinds of loaf from Africa turn up on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' looks like food, matching the surface, but it is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Brands are kinds of product sold under one maker's name, so the word means sorts or types.

clue.text: Lacking independence those kids arranged places to work flexibly

indicators.note: lacking something means it is missing, so a letter is removed
arranged means set out in a fresh order

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for independent or independence
taken as written

explanation.surface: Children without freedom are seated where they can do schoolwork at any time.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot desks are workstations shared by whoever needs one, with no permanent owner, suiting staff on varying schedules.

clue.text: One who tries assorted treats

indicators.note: assorted means mixed up, so the letters come in a jumbled order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone samples a selection of sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster samples food or drink to judge its quality, so the person tries things out by tasting.

clue.text: Criticise return of head man

indicators.note: the return of something sends it back the way it came, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: conk is slang for the head or nose
K is the king, a chess man

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the boss coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the head is turned round; the chessman's K stays put at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone is informal for running them down or finding fault, as in knocking a rival's work.

clue.text: Stew brother has for part of breakfast?

blocks.note: a hash is a stew of chopped meat
Br is the abbreviation for brother
to own is to have

explanation.surface: A sibling eats stew as his morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: hash browns are only one possible part of a breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash browns are fried patties of grated potato, a common item in a cooked morning fry-up.

clue.text: It goes round and round in dance

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a hop is an informal dance
a round letter shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Something keeps spinning during a dance, like a whirling dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a ring, which encircles things, and a hula hoop is spun around the waist.

clue.text: Cultivate Dutch Elm?

blocks.note: to cultivate someone is to court their favour
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A gardener is told to grow the tree hit by Dutch elm disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivate Dutch Elm' recalls Dutch elm disease, so the solver reads gardening; cultivate means woo, and the question mark flags elm as one example of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a hardwood timber used for furniture and coffins, so it is one example of the material.

clue.text: Small round sweet with hole

blocks.note: first meaning: a little boiled sweet
second meaning: in golf, to sink a putt

explanation.surface: A tiny ring-shaped mint has a gap in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Polo mint with its hole, but hole is a verb from golf: to drop a putt is to hole it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear drop is a small boiled confection, and golfers speak of dropping a putt when they sink it in the cup.

clue.text: Gem of a joke by pious person

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces are set side by side

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
as in 'have you heard the one about...'

explanation.surface: A devout person tells a splendid joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gem of a joke' reads as praise for a joke, but Gem is the definition and 'of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious jewels such as rubies and diamonds are called stones, so the word stands for a jewel.

clue.text: Deranged bloke holds one small dagger

indicators.note: deranged means thrown out of order, so the letters are scrambled
something that holds another keeps it inside

blocks.note: the letters of bloke rearranged
I is one, S is small

explanation.surface: A madman carries a single little knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dagger' is the printer's mark that looks like a small cross, and its old name is the word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: In typography the obelisk or obelus is the dagger symbol used to mark footnotes, a printing sense of the word.
